profile.industry: Clinical diagnostics laboratory network and patient results portal
profile.prior_audit_scope: The prior engagement was the SOC 2 Type II examination of the results platform and supporting infrastructure covering security, availability and confidentiality for the period 2025-07-01 to 2026-06-30. It did not cover the laboratory information system interfaces, the retention and disposal controls, or the third-party oversight programme, and it expressed no opinion on compliance with 11 CCR §§ 7121-7124.
profile.audit_scope_rationale: The audit covers the multi-tenant results platform, the laboratory information system interfaces, the patient portal and the corporate identity estate — every system recorded in the CMDB as holding patient personal information. The 2026 SOC 2 Type II report (period 2025-07-01 to 2026-06-30, issued 2026-07-24) and the ISO 27001 certificate (issued 2025-11-03) are leveraged as permitted, and the components those engagements do not directly test — segmentation boundaries, retention and disposal, and third-party oversight — are tested independently by the auditor against the § 7123(c) component list.
profile.auditor_engagement_status: External auditor engaged, independence confirmed in writing

controls.label: Authentication
controls.notes: Okta is the sole identity provider for all 1,180 workforce accounts and all four production consoles; phishing-resistant FIDO2 keys are mandatory for the 41 administrative roles and TOTP for everyone else, with password authentication disabled at the directory. The IAM lead (Director of Identity Engineering) owns the policy, reviews the authenticator inventory monthly, and Okta ThreatInsight alerts route to the 24x7 on-call queue. Evidence: the signed authentication standard (v6, 2026-05-18), an Okta policy export dated 2026-07-02, and the July 2026 authenticator-coverage report showing 100% enrolment.

controls.label: Encryption of personal information
controls.notes: All personal information is encrypted at rest with AES-256 under customer-scoped AWS KMS keys (RDS, Aurora, S3, EBS snapshots) and in transit with TLS 1.3, minimum TLS 1.2 for two legacy partner endpoints documented in the exception register. The Principal Platform Security Engineer owns key rotation on a 365-day schedule, and AWS Config rule 'encrypted-volumes' plus a nightly S3 bucket sweep alert on any unencrypted object within 15 minutes. Evidence: the encryption standard (v4, 2026-03-09), KMS key-policy exports of 2026-06-30, and the Config compliance report for July 2026.

controls.label: Account management and access controls
controls.notes: Access is role-based across 34 defined roles provisioned by SCIM from Workday, with just-in-time elevation for production through Teleport capped at four hours and dual approval. Joiner-mover-leaver runs automatically on the Workday event with a 30-minute deprovisioning SLA measured monthly (June 2026 median: 6 minutes); the IT Operations Manager owns the process and the Security Governance Manager runs the quarterly certification of every privileged role. Evidence: the access-control procedure (v5, 2026-04-21), the Q2 2026 access-certification pack signed 2026-07-08, and Teleport session logs.

controls.label: Inventory and management of personal information and systems
controls.notes: A single asset and data inventory lives in ServiceNow CMDB, reconciled nightly against AWS Config, Azure Resource Graph and Jamf so that unmanaged assets surface within 24 hours; 612 systems and 41 data stores are recorded, each with an owner, a data-category tag and a retention class. BigID scans the data stores weekly for personal information and writes classifications back to the CMDB record. The Data Governance Manager owns the inventory and attests to its completeness quarterly. Evidence: the inventory procedure (v3, 2026-02-16), the 2026-07-01 CMDB export, and the Q2 attestation.

controls.label: Secure configuration of hardware and software
controls.notes: CIS Benchmark Level 1 baselines are enforced for Ubuntu 22.04 hosts, EKS nodes and macOS endpoints through Ansible and Jamf, with drift detection by AWS Config and Wiz posture rules alerting to the platform channel within one hour. Deviations require a recorded exception approved by the Head of Platform Engineering with a 90-day expiry; eleven exceptions are open and all carry expiry dates. The Head of Platform Engineering owns the baselines and re-baselines every six months. Evidence: the hardening standard (v7, 2026-06-02), Ansible role definitions, and the July 2026 drift report.

controls.label: Vulnerability scanning and penetration testing
controls.notes: Wiz performs continuous cloud and container scanning and Tenable performs authenticated weekly scans of all endpoints and hosts; remediation SLAs are 7 days critical, 30 days high, 90 days medium, tracked as Jira tickets with automatic escalation to the Head of Security at 80% of SLA. An independent penetration test of the production platform and mobile clients was completed by an external firm on 2026-05-22 with two medium findings, both remediated and retested on 2026-06-19. The Vulnerability Management Lead owns the programme. Evidence: the 2026-05-22 test report and retest letter, and the July 2026 SLA-attainment report (97.4%).

controls.label: Audit-log management
controls.notes: CloudTrail (all regions, organisation trail), VPC flow logs, EKS audit logs, database audit logs and application access logs ship to Splunk Cloud with 400-day hot retention and 7-year archive in S3 Object Lock; logs are write-once and the security team holds no delete rights. Log-source health is monitored by a Splunk saved search that pages on-call if any source stops for more than 30 minutes. The Detection Engineering Lead owns coverage and reviews the source roster monthly. Evidence: the logging standard (v4, 2026-01-27), the Splunk index-retention configuration export, and the July 2026 source-health report.

controls.label: Network monitoring and defenses
controls.notes: AWS GuardDuty, VPC flow-log analytics and Cloudflare WAF/DDoS protection front every internet-facing service, with detections normalised into Splunk Enterprise Security where 63 correlation rules run continuously; the 24x7 managed detection provider triages and escalates to internal on-call under a 15-minute critical acknowledgement SLA. The Detection Engineering Lead tunes rules fortnightly and reports mean-time-to-acknowledge monthly (June 2026: 4 minutes). Evidence: the monitoring runbook (v6, 2026-05-05), the MDR service report for June 2026, and GuardDuty configuration exports.

controls.label: Antivirus and anti-malware protections
controls.notes: CrowdStrike Falcon is deployed on 100% of the 1,240 managed endpoints and all 612 server workloads, enforced at enrolment by Jamf and by an EKS admission controller that blocks unprotected nodes; prevention policies are set to aggressive with automatic quarantine and host isolation. Coverage is reconciled daily against the CMDB and any gap over 24 hours pages the IT Operations Manager, who owns the control. Evidence: the endpoint-protection standard (v3, 2026-04-02), the 2026-07-01 Falcon coverage export showing 100%, and the June 2026 detection summary.

controls.label: Segmentation of an information system
controls.notes: Production, staging and corporate environments sit in separate AWS accounts under distinct organisational units with no peering; the data tier runs in private subnets reachable only from application security groups, and east-west traffic inside EKS is constrained by Cilium network policies in default-deny. Corporate access to production is only via the Teleport bastion. The Head of Platform Engineering owns the topology and reviews segmentation boundaries semi-annually; the last review was 2026-04-30 and produced two accepted findings now closed. Evidence: the network-architecture document (v5, 2026-04-30), Terraform account structure, and Cilium policy exports.

controls.label: Port and protocol management and protection
controls.notes: Security groups and network ACLs are deny-by-default and defined exclusively in Terraform; every permitted port and protocol is registered in the CMDB with a business justification and a named owner, and any pull request opening a port to 0.0.0.0/0 is blocked by a Checkov policy gate requiring Head of Security approval. Wiz flags exposed ports continuously and the platform team clears findings within seven days. The Head of Platform Engineering owns the register and reviews it quarterly; the last review was 2026-06-12. Evidence: the port register export of 2026-06-12, Terraform modules, and the Checkov policy configuration.

controls.label: Cybersecurity awareness
controls.notes: Monthly phishing simulations run through KnowBe4 across the whole workforce (June 2026 click rate 1.9%, report rate 62%), with immediate micro-training for anyone who clicks and manager escalation on a third failure in twelve months. Quarterly threat-landscape briefings are delivered by the Head of Security to all staff and separately to the executive team, and a security-champions network of 22 engineers meets monthly. The People Operations Director co-owns completion tracking with the Head of Security. Evidence: KnowBe4 campaign reports for 2026, the briefing deck of 2026-06-24, and completion records.

controls.label: Cybersecurity education and training
controls.notes: Role-based training is mandatory: general security and privacy training within 14 days of hire and annually thereafter (2026 completion 100% of 1,180 staff as of 2026-06-30), secure-coding training annually for the 214 engineers, and incident-handling training for the 31 responders. Completion is enforced by Workday learning assignments with manager escalation at 21 days overdue and access review at 45 days. The People Operations Director owns delivery and the Head of Security owns curriculum, refreshed each January. Evidence: the training standard (v4, 2026-01-15), the 2026-06-30 completion report, and course records.

controls.label: Secure development and coding practices
controls.notes: The SDLC requires threat modelling for every new service and every change to an authentication or data-export path, peer review by a second engineer, and a CI gate running Semgrep SAST, Snyk SCA and Trivy image scanning that fails the build on any high or critical finding; secrets scanning by Gitleaks runs pre-commit and in CI. Production deploys are automated, signed and traceable to a reviewed commit. The Director of Engineering owns the SDLC standard with the Head of Security as approver; it was last revised 2026-03-30. Evidence: the SDLC standard (v8), CI pipeline definitions, and the June 2026 gate-failure report.

controls.label: Oversight of service providers, contractors, and third parties
controls.notes: All 68 vendors are recorded in the OneTrust third-party register with a tier, a business owner and a data-flow description; the 19 vendors that process personal information are tier-1 and require a signed data-processing agreement with CCPA service-provider terms, an annual SOC 2 Type II or ISO 27001 certificate review, and evidence of subcontractor controls. Onboarding is gated by the Vendor Risk Manager and no production data may be shared before approval; offboarding includes documented deletion certification. Reviews are annual, and all 19 tier-1 reviews for 2026 closed by 2026-06-30. Evidence: the register export, executed agreements, and 2026 certificate reviews.

controls.label: Retention schedules and proper disposal of personal information
controls.notes: The retention schedule assigns every one of the 41 data stores a retention class tied to the purpose that sets it — operational service records 24 months after account closure, billing records seven years under tax obligations, support transcripts 18 months — and deletion is executed automatically by S3 lifecycle rules and a nightly database purge job, with deletion receipts written to an audit table. Media disposal uses certified destruction with certificates retained. The Data Governance Manager owns the schedule, last approved 2026-02-16, and samples deletion evidence quarterly. Evidence: the schedule, purge-job logs, and destruction certificates.

controls.label: Security-incident response management
controls.notes: The incident-response plan defines four severity levels, a named incident commander rota of six, and notification decision points with counsel for CCPA and state breach obligations; PagerDuty carries a 15-minute acknowledgement SLA for Sev-1 and Sev-2. Playbooks cover ransomware, credential compromise, vendor breach and data exfiltration. One Sev-3 incident occurred in the last twelve months (a vendor-side exposure with no personal information involved), closed on 2026-02-11 with three corrective actions all completed. A tabletop exercise ran 2026-05-14. The Head of Security owns the plan (v9, 2026-05-20). Evidence: the plan, the incident record, and the tabletop after-action report.

controls.label: Business-continuity and disaster-recovery planning
controls.notes: The business-continuity and disaster-recovery plan sets an RTO of four hours and an RPO of fifteen minutes for the production platform, supported by multi-AZ Aurora with cross-region replicas to us-west-2 and immutable backups in S3 Object Lock; restoration is exercised monthly against a scratch account and a full cross-region failover was exercised on 2026-04-18, meeting RTO in 2 hours 41 minutes. Backup integrity is verified automatically after every snapshot. The VP of Infrastructure owns the plan (v6, 2026-04-25) and reviews it annually with the executive team. Evidence: the plan, the 2026-04-18 failover report, and monthly restore-test logs.

controls.finding: The operative requirement assessed here is 11 CCR § 7123(c)(1). For comparative context, the HIPAA Security Rule addresses authentication controls for electronic protected health information under 45 CFR Part 164, Subpart C; that framework is referenced for orientation only and does not alter the operative standard.
controls.remediation: Retain and make audit-ready the authentication standard (v6, 2026-05-18), the 2026-07-02 Okta policy export, and the July 2026 100%-enrollment authenticator-coverage report as the evidentiary record for this component, per the five-year audit-record retention requirement. Confirm that the monthly authenticator-inventory review process produces a durable log entry the auditor can examine for each review cycle, and that Okta ThreatInsight alert records are retained in Splunk alongside the coverage reports. Retain the determination of FIDO2 coverage scope — specifically, confirm that the 41 administrative roles enumerated in the coverage report align exactly with every privileged account identified in the account-management control — so the auditor can cross-validate phishing-resistant MFA scope against the privileged-account register without gap.

controls.finding: The intake establishes encryption of personal information at rest and in transit: AES-256 under customer-scoped AWS KMS keys protects RDS, Aurora, S3, and EBS snapshots; TLS 1.3 is enforced in transit with TLS 1.2 permitted only for two legacy partner endpoints documented in a formal exception register. Key rotation runs on a 365-day schedule owned by the Principal Platform Security Engineer, and automated controls — AWS Config rule 'encrypted-volumes' and a nightly S3 bucket sweep — alert within 15 minutes on any unencrypted object. The encryption standard (v4, 2026-03-09), KMS key-policy exports dated 2026-06-30, and the July 2026 Config compliance report substantiate continuous monitoring. For comparative context, the HIPAA Security Rule addresses encryption of electronic protected health information under 45 CFR Part 164, Subpart C; the operative requirement assessed here is the encryption component of the cybersecurity audit.
controls.remediation: Retain and make audit-ready the encryption standard (v4, 2026-03-09), the 2026-06-30 KMS key-policy exports, and the July 2026 AWS Config compliance report for this component, per the five-year audit-record retention requirement. Retain the exception-register entries for the two legacy partner endpoints that accept TLS 1.2, including the documented business justification, the named owner, and the expiry date for each exception, so the auditor can assess the adequacy of the exception-management process without reliance solely on management assertion. Confirm that the nightly S3 bucket sweep produces a retained alert log the auditor can inspect for each review cycle, in addition to the monthly Config compliance report.

controls.finding: The operative requirement assessed here is 11 CCR § 7123(c)(3). For comparative context, the HIPAA Security Rule addresses access controls and workforce clearance procedures for electronic protected health information under 45 CFR Part 164, Subpart C; that framework is referenced for orientation only and does not alter the operative standard.
controls.remediation: Retain and make audit-ready the access-control procedure (v5, 2026-04-21), the Q2 2026 signed access-certification pack (signed 2026-07-08), and Teleport session logs evidencing just-in-time elevation and dual-approval enforcement, per the five-year audit-record retention requirement. Retain the monthly deprovisioning-SLA measurement records — including the June 2026 median figure of 6 minutes — in a durable log the auditor can examine across successive periods, not only for the most recent cycle. Confirm that the quarterly privileged-role certification scope covers all 34 RBAC roles and that the certification pack records the certifier's identity, the date, and any exceptions or remediation actions, so the auditor can assess the adequacy of the certification process without reliance on management attestation alone.

controls.finding: The intake establishes a centralized asset and data inventory in ServiceNow CMDB, reconciled nightly against AWS Config, Azure Resource Graph, and Jamf, with unmanaged assets surfacing within 24 hours; 612 systems and 41 data stores are recorded, each with an owner, a data-category tag, and a retention class. BigID performs weekly scans of the data stores for personal information and writes classifications back to the CMDB record. The Data Governance Manager owns the inventory and attests to its completeness quarterly. The inventory element under this component covers the patient health and diagnostic personal information processed across the 41 data stores and 612 systems identified in the intake, including the multi-tenant results platform, the laboratory information system interfaces, the patient portal, and the corporate identity estate recorded in the CMDB. The inventory procedure (v3, 2026-02-16), the 2026-07-01 CMDB export, and the Q2 attestation substantiate the control.
controls.remediation: Retain and make audit-ready the inventory procedure (v3, 2026-02-16), the 2026-07-01 CMDB export, and the Q2 Data Governance Manager completeness attestation for this component, per the five-year audit-record retention requirement. Confirm that the allowlisting configuration — specifically, the discrete lists of authorized hardware and software controlling what is permitted to connect to and execute on the information system — is documented as a separately identifiable artefact in the CMDB or a linked record, because the intake describes asset discovery and classification but does not explicitly address allowlisting; the auditor must examine allowlisting evidence independently of the broader inventory. Retain BigID weekly scan outputs as a time-series log rather than only the most recent report, so the auditor can assess the continuity of the personal-information classification process across the audit period.

controls.finding: The intake establishes a mature secure-configuration program: CIS Benchmark Level 1 baselines are enforced for Ubuntu 22.04 hosts, EKS nodes, and macOS endpoints via Ansible and Jamf; drift is detected by AWS Config and Wiz posture rules alerting within one hour; deviations require a recorded exception approved by the Head of Platform Engineering with a 90-day expiry; eleven exceptions are currently open, all carrying documented expiry dates. For comparative context, the HIPAA Security Rule addresses workstation and device security under 45 CFR Part 164, Subpart C; the operative requirement assessed here is the secure-configuration component of the cybersecurity audit.
controls.remediation: Retain and make audit-ready the hardening standard (v7, 2026-06-02), Ansible role definitions, and the July 2026 drift report as the evidentiary record for this component, per the five-year audit-record retention requirement. Retain the eleven open exception records — including each exception's approval date, approver identity, business justification, and 90-day expiry — in a durable register the auditor can examine; the audit must assess the exception-management process against the change-management and configuration-integrity requirements, and the auditor cannot rely on management assertion alone. Confirm that the intake's hardening standard separately addresses masking of sensitive personal information in applications, as required by the secure-configuration component; the intake notes do not explicitly reference an application-masking control, and the auditor will need to examine that sub-element independently.

controls.finding: The intake establishes a mature vulnerability-management and penetration-testing program: Wiz performs continuous cloud and container scanning; Tenable performs authenticated weekly scans of all endpoints and hosts; remediation SLAs are tiered at 7 days (critical), 30 days (high), and 90 days (medium), tracked as Jira tickets with automatic escalation to the Head of Security at 80% of SLA; a July 2026 SLA-attainment report records 97.4% compliance. An independent external penetration test of the production platform and mobile clients was completed on 2026-05-22 with two medium findings, both remediated and retested by 2026-06-19. The Vulnerability Management Lead owns the program. The 2026-05-22 test report, retest letter, and the July 2026 SLA-attainment report substantiate the control.
controls.remediation: Retain and make audit-ready the 2026-05-22 external penetration test report, the 2026-06-19 retest letter confirming remediation of both medium findings, and the July 2026 SLA-attainment report (97.4%) as the primary evidentiary record for this component, per the five-year audit-record retention requirement. Retain the Jira ticket history for SLA-tracked vulnerabilities — including escalation records for tickets reaching the 80%-of-SLA threshold — as a time-series log across the full audit period, not only the most recent monthly snapshot, so the auditor can assess the continuity of the remediation process. Confirm whether the business operates a vulnerability-disclosure or bug-bounty program; the intake does not address this sub-element, and the auditor will need to assess it or document its non-applicability.

controls.finding: The operative requirement assessed here is 11 CCR § 7123(c)(7). For comparative context, the HIPAA Security Rule addresses audit controls for electronic protected health information under 45 CFR Part 164, Subpart C, and FDA 21 CFR Part 11 addresses audit-trail requirements for electronic records on clinical systems; those frameworks are referenced for orientation only and do not alter the operative standard.
controls.remediation: Retain and make audit-ready the logging standard (v4, 2026-01-27), the Splunk index-retention configuration export, and the July 2026 source-health report as the evidentiary record for this component, per the five-year audit-record retention requirement. Retain the monthly source-roster review records produced by the Detection Engineering Lead — not only the most recent report — so the auditor can assess coverage continuity across the audit period. Confirm that the seven-year S3 Object Lock archive retention period and the 400-day Splunk hot-tier retention period are each documented in the logging standard or a separate data-retention schedule, with a named owner and a documented basis, so the auditor can assess the adequacy of the retention configuration against the audit period without relying solely on the configuration export.

controls.finding: The operative requirement assessed here is 11 CCR § 7123(c)(8). For comparative context, the HIPAA Security Rule addresses audit controls and integrity safeguards for electronic protected health information under 45 CFR Part 164, Subpart C; that framework is referenced for orientation only and does not alter the operative standard.
controls.remediation: Retain and make audit-ready the monitoring runbook (v6, 2026-05-05), the June 2026 MDR service report, and the GuardDuty configuration exports as the evidentiary record for this component, per the five-year audit-record retention requirement. Retain the monthly mean-time-to-acknowledge reports across the full audit period — not only the June 2026 snapshot — so the auditor can assess the continuity of the 15-minute critical SLA over time. Confirm whether a data-loss-prevention system is deployed in addition to the detection and prevention technologies listed in the intake; the intake identifies GuardDuty, flow-log analytics, WAF, and MDR correlation rules but does not explicitly identify a DLP solution, and the auditor will need to assess that sub-element or document its non-applicability.

controls.finding: The operative requirement assessed here is 11 CCR § 7123(c)(9). For comparative context, the HIPAA Security Rule addresses malicious software protection for electronic protected health information under 45 CFR Part 164, Subpart C; that framework is referenced for orientation only and does not alter the operative standard.
controls.remediation: Retain and make audit-ready the endpoint-protection standard (v3, 2026-04-02), the 2026-07-01 Falcon coverage export showing 100% across 1,240 endpoints and 612 server workloads, and the June 2026 detection summary as the evidentiary record for this component, per the five-year audit-record retention requirement. Retain the daily CMDB-reconciliation logs — including records of any gap-alert events and their resolution — as a time-series record across the full audit period, so the auditor can assess the continuity of 100% coverage and the responsiveness of the gap-remediation process without relying on a single point-in-time export. Confirm that the EKS admission controller configuration is captured in a version-controlled policy document alongside the Jamf enrollment rule, so the auditor can examine the enforcement mechanism for both endpoint classes as a single, coherent evidentiary set.

controls.finding: The intake establishes a multi-layered segmentation architecture: production, staging, and corporate environments occupy separate AWS accounts under distinct organizational units with no peering, the data tier runs in private subnets accessible only from designated application security groups, east-west traffic inside EKS is constrained by Cilium network policies operating in default-deny mode, and corporate access to production is exclusively via the Teleport bastion. The Head of Platform Engineering owns the topology, conducts semi-annual boundary reviews — the most recent on 2026-04-30 — and the prior review produced two findings, both now closed, demonstrating a functioning improvement cycle. The final regulation lists segmentation of the information system as a standalone audit component and does not list zero-trust architecture as a separate requirement; segmentation must be independently evidenced on its own terms, in addition to any broader architectural controls in place, and the network-architecture document (v5, 2026-04-30), Terraform account-structure files, and Cilium policy exports constitute the auditable segmentation record.
controls.remediation: Retain and make audit-ready the network-architecture document (v5, 2026-04-30), the Terraform account-structure files, and the Cilium network-policy exports as implemented in the multi-account AWS environment, evidencing the segment scope, zone definitions, and boundary-enforcement mechanisms for the production, staging, and corporate accounts; retain these artifacts per the five-year audit-record retention rule at 11 CCR § 7122(g). Before the applicable first-audit deadline, confirm that the semi-annual boundary review scheduled for late 2026 is completed and documented, with any new findings tracked to closure as the 2026-04-30 findings were. Verify that the Teleport bastion session logs covering corporate-to-production access paths are also retained as part of the segmentation evidence package, since boundary enforcement is only as strong as the access-path controls that backstop it.

controls.finding: The intake establishes that security groups and network ACLs are deny-by-default and defined exclusively in Terraform; every permitted port and protocol is registered in the ServiceNow CMDB with a business justification and a named owner; a Checkov policy gate blocks any pull request opening a port to 0.0.0.0/0 and requires Head of Security approval to override; Wiz flags exposed ports continuously with a seven-day clearance SLA for the platform team; and the Head of Platform Engineering owns and reviews the register quarterly, with the most recent review completed 2026-06-12. The port register export of 2026-06-12, Terraform modules, and Checkov policy configuration collectively constitute an auditable, enforcement-evidenced record for this component.
controls.remediation: Retain and make audit-ready the port register export dated 2026-06-12, the Terraform security-group modules, and the Checkov policy configuration as implemented in the multi-account AWS environment, evidencing both the deny-by-default posture and the approval workflow for any exception; retain these artifacts per 11 CCR § 7122(g). Confirm that the next quarterly register review (due approximately 2026-09-12) produces a timestamped sign-off by the Head of Platform Engineering, which the auditor will require to evidence continuous operation rather than a point-in-time snapshot. Add to the audit package the Wiz finding-clearance log showing the seven-day SLA attainment for exposed-port findings, as that log demonstrates the monitoring-and-remediation cycle that distinguishes a managed port posture from a static rule set.

controls.finding: The business must retain documentation that separately evidences awareness activities — such as threat advisories, phishing simulation results, or security-culture communications — distinct from formal training curricula, so that the auditor can assess the two components independently. The intake supplies that documentation: monthly KnowBe4 phishing simulations across the full workforce (June 2026 click rate 1.9%, report rate 62%), immediate micro-training triggered on any click, manager escalation on a third failure in twelve months, quarterly threat-landscape briefings by the Head of Security to all staff and separately to the executive team, and a 22-engineer security-champions network meeting monthly. The People Operations Director co-owns completion tracking with the Head of Security. If the retained documentation does not separately label awareness activities apart from the role-based training program addressed under the education and training component, the auditor cannot assess this component independently; the business should confirm that the KnowBe4 campaign reports, briefing decks, and security-champions records are filed as a discrete awareness evidence set.
controls.remediation: Retain and make audit-ready the KnowBe4 campaign reports for calendar year 2026 (capturing monthly simulation metrics including the June 2026 1.9% click rate and 62% report rate), the threat-landscape briefing deck dated 2026-06-24, and the security-champions meeting records — filed as a discrete awareness evidence package separate from the training-completion records used for the education and training component — per the five-year audit-record retention rule at 11 CCR § 7122(g). Confirm that the micro-training trigger logs (recording which accounts received immediate follow-up and on what date) are retained alongside the simulation reports, since the auditor will examine the consequence-and-remediation loop, not only the simulation headline metrics. Ensure the quarterly threat-briefing cadence produces a dated attendance or distribution record for each session so the briefing frequency and audience coverage can be independently verified.

controls.finding: The business must retain documentation that separately evidences formal training activities — such as structured onboarding, annual training completion records, or role-based curricula — distinct from general awareness activities, so that the auditor can assess this component independently. The intake supplies that documentation: mandatory general security and privacy training within 14 days of hire and annually thereafter with 100% completion across 1,180 staff as of 2026-06-30; annual secure-coding training for the 214 engineers; incident-handling training for the 31 responders; completion enforced by Workday learning assignments with manager escalation at 21 days overdue and access review at 45 days; and curriculum owned by the Head of Security and refreshed each January. The People Operations Director owns delivery. The training standard (v4, 2026-01-15), the 2026-06-30 completion report, and course records constitute the auditable training record for this component. The regulation also requires training after a personal information security breach; the intake records one incident in the twelve-month period (a Sev-3 vendor-side exposure with no personal information involved, closed 2026-02-11), and the three corrective actions documented for that incident should be confirmed to include any applicable post-incident training trigger.
controls.remediation: Retain and make audit-ready the training standard (v4, 2026-01-15), the 2026-06-30 completion report showing 100% of 1,180 staff, the engineer-specific secure-coding training records for the 214-person engineering population, and the incident-responder training records for the 31 responders — filed separately from the KnowBe4 awareness campaign records used for the cybersecurity awareness component — per 11 CCR § 7122(g). Confirm in the incident record for the 2026-02-11 Sev-3 closure whether any post-incident training obligation was triggered and, if so, that a completion record was generated; this confirmation resolves the one open question on this component before the audit. Before the January 2027 curriculum refresh, document the scope of any changes so the auditor can verify the refresh occurred on the stated annual cadence.

controls.finding: further clarification is advisable regarding whether any production systems in the CMDB are subject to FDA 21 CFR Part 11 obligations, and if so, whether the SDLC standard's review and testing requirements satisfy Part 11 validation documentation requirements for those systems.
controls.remediation: Retain and make audit-ready the SDLC standard (v8, 2026-03-30), the CI pipeline definitions for the Semgrep, Snyk, Trivy, and Gitleaks gates, and the June 2026 gate-failure report as implemented in the production deploy pipeline — supplemented by a code-review coverage report showing the proportion of commits that received peer review in the audit period, and a log or ticket summary of threat models completed for new services and authentication/data-export path changes; these two additions close the foreseeable auditor inquiry noted in the finding, and all artifacts should be retained per 11 CCR § 7122(g). If any systems in the ServiceNow CMDB are classified as subject to FDA 21 CFR Part 11, confirm that the SDLC validation-documentation requirements for those systems are addressed in the standard or in a supplemental procedure before the audit is conducted. Ensure the next annual SDLC revision (following the 2026-03-30 version) is dated and signed by both the Director of Engineering and the Head of Security to evidence the dual-ownership review cadence.

controls.finding: The intake establishes that all 68 vendors are recorded in the OneTrust third-party register with a tier designation, a business owner, and a data-flow description; the 19 vendors that process personal information are classified as tier-1 and require a signed data-processing agreement containing CCPA service-provider terms, an annual SOC 2 Type II or ISO 27001 certificate review, and evidence of subcontractor controls. The operative requirement is 11 CCR § 7123(c)(15). Onboarding is gated by the Vendor Risk Manager and no production data may be shared before approval; offboarding includes documented deletion certification. All 19 tier-1 reviews for 2026 closed by 2026-06-30. The prior SOC 2 Type II engagement covering 2025-07-01 to 2026-06-30 expressly excluded the third-party oversight program from scope and expressed no opinion on it; the auditor therefore tested this component independently, consistent with the audit-scope rationale. The intake does not indicate whether the 49 tier-2 and tier-3 vendors that do not process personal information are subject to any periodic reassessment to confirm their tier classification remains accurate — if a vendor's data-processing activity changes without a corresponding tier reclassification, the program's coverage boundary becomes unreliable; further internal investigation is advisable regarding the tier-reassessment cadence for non-tier-1 vendors.
controls.remediation: Retain and make audit-ready the OneTrust register export, the 19 executed tier-1 data-processing agreements, and the 2026 SOC 2 Type II or ISO 27001 certificate reviews for each tier-1 vendor as the primary oversight-program evidence, along with deletion certifications for any offboarded tier-1 vendors in the audit period — all retained per 11 CCR § 7122(g). Produce and retain documentation of the process by which the Vendor Risk Manager reassesses tier-2 and tier-3 vendors when their data-processing activity changes, including the trigger event and the escalation path if a vendor's activity expands to include personal information; this closes the open question regarding the 49 non-tier-1 vendors. Confirm that the subcontractor-controls evidence collected from tier-1 vendors during the 2026 annual reviews is retained in the OneTrust record or a linked document repository so the auditor can examine it without requiring a second vendor contact.

controls.finding: The intake establishes that each of the 41 data stores recorded in the ServiceNow CMDB carries a retention class tied to the purpose that sets it — operational service records 24 months after account closure, billing records seven years under tax obligations, and support transcripts 18 months — with deletion executed automatically by S3 lifecycle rules and a nightly database purge job; deletion receipts are written to an audit table. Media disposal uses certified destruction with certificates retained. The Data Governance Manager owns the schedule, last approved 2026-02-16, and samples deletion evidence quarterly. For comparative context, the prior SOC 2 Type II engagement expressly excluded retention and disposal controls from its scope; the auditor therefore tested this component independently; the operative requirement is 11 CCR § 7123(c)(16). The intake does not specify whether the retention schedule covers all personal information categories held in the results platform and laboratory information system interfaces — including any diagnostic data, health records, or patient identifiers processed through the LIS interfaces — or whether the 41 data stores in the CMDB are the complete universe of stores holding patient personal information; further internal investigation is advisable regarding whether any LIS-interface data stores are recorded in the CMDB and assigned a retention class.
controls.remediation: Retain and make audit-ready the approved retention schedule (last approved 2026-02-16), the S3 lifecycle-rule configurations and nightly purge-job logs for all 41 CMDB-recorded data stores, the deletion-receipt audit table entries from the audit period, and the certified media-destruction certificates — all as implemented across the multi-tenant results platform, the laboratory information system interfaces, and the patient portal — per the five-year audit-record retention requirement at 11 CCR § 7122(g), in support of the operative component requirement at 11 CCR § 7123(c)(16). Before the audit, confirm with the Data Governance Manager that the CMDB's 41 data-store records are the complete inventory of stores holding patient personal information, including any stores accessed via the LIS interfaces; if any LIS-interface data stores are not yet assigned a retention class, document them and assign classes before the audit period closes. Ensure the next quarterly deletion-evidence sample (due approximately Q3 2026) produces a signed attestation from the Data Governance Manager referencing the specific purge-job runs reviewed, so the auditor can trace the sampling process end-to-end.

controls.finding: The intake establishes a fully documented incident-response capability: the plan (v9, 2026-05-20) defines four severity levels, a named incident-commander rota of six, and notification decision points with counsel for CCPA and state breach obligations; PagerDuty carries a 15-minute acknowledgement SLA for Sev-1 and Sev-2; playbooks cover ransomware, credential compromise, vendor breach, and data exfiltration; a tabletop exercise ran 2026-05-14. One Sev-3 incident occurred in the twelve-month period — a vendor-side exposure with no personal information involved, closed 2026-02-11 with three corrective actions all completed. The intake reports incidents in the last 12 months; the incident-response component is anchored to that record. Because no personal information was involved in the Sev-3 incident, Cal. Civ. Code § 1798.82(a)'s individual-notification duty and § 1798.82(f)'s Attorney General submission duty (triggered for breaches affecting more than 500 California residents, requiring electronic submission of a sample notification to the AG within 15 calendar days of notifying affected consumers) were not triggered on the facts stated; however, the incident record should confirm that this determination was made and documented at the time of closure, and the plan's notification decision points should be retained as evidence that the process for making that determination exists. The audit report must also include, where applicable, a sample or description of any Cal. Code § 1798.82(a) consumer notifications and any notifications to California agencies with jurisdiction over privacy laws, per 11 CCR § 7123(e).
controls.remediation: Retain and make audit-ready the incident-response plan (v9, 2026-05-20), all four playbooks (ransomware, credential compromise, vendor breach, data exfiltration), the 2026-05-14 tabletop after-action report, the 2026-02-11 Sev-3 incident record with the three corrective-action closure evidence items, and PagerDuty SLA attainment logs — as implemented across the multi-tenant results platform and corporate identity estate — per 11 CCR § 7122(g). Confirm that the 2026-02-11 incident record contains a documented determination that no personal information was involved and therefore no Cal. Civ. Code § 1798.82 notification obligation was triggered; retain that determination as part of the incident record so the auditor can verify the notification-decision process without reliance on management attestation alone, consistent with 11 CCR § 7122(d). Schedule the next tabletop or functional exercise before the first-audit coverage period closes, and retain the after-action report as evidence of the ongoing testing cadence required by the enumerated component.

controls.finding: The intake establishes a business-continuity and disaster-recovery plan (v6, 2026-04-25) setting an RTO of four hours and an RPO of fifteen minutes for the production platform, supported by multi-AZ Aurora with cross-region replicas to us-west-2 and immutable backups in S3 Object Lock; restoration is exercised monthly against a scratch account and a full cross-region failover was exercised on 2026-04-18, meeting RTO in 2 hours 41 minutes; backup integrity is verified automatically after every snapshot. The VP of Infrastructure owns the plan and reviews it annually with the executive team. The plan (v6), the 2026-04-18 failover report, and monthly restore-test logs form the core audit-ready package. The intake does not address whether the business-continuity plan covers the laboratory information system interfaces and the patient portal as distinct recovery targets with their own RTO/RPO objectives, or whether the four-hour RTO applies uniformly to all in-scope systems including the LIS interfaces; further internal investigation is advisable regarding whether the BC/DR plan separately documents recovery objectives for each system category identified in the audit scope.
controls.remediation: Retain and make audit-ready the BC/DR plan (v6, 2026-04-25), the 2026-04-18 cross-region failover test report confirming RTO attainment in 2 hours 41 minutes, the monthly restore-test logs for the audit period, and the S3 Object Lock backup configuration — as implemented for the multi-AZ Aurora production platform replicating to us-west-2 — per 11 CCR § 7122(g). Confirm with the VP of Infrastructure whether the BC/DR plan assigns distinct RTO and RPO objectives to the laboratory information system interfaces and the patient portal as separate recovery targets; if those systems share the production-platform objectives, document that scope decision explicitly in the plan so the auditor can assess coverage without ambiguity. Ensure the annual executive-team review of the plan (following the 2026-04-25 version) produces a dated sign-off record, since the auditor will require evidence of the review cadence rather than the plan version date alone.

top_risks.title: Audit-evidence packaging gap across three Implemented-rated controls
top_risks.deadline: Prior to the formal audit engagement commencing under 11 CCR § 7122; first audit report due by the applicable April 1 phase-in date under 11 CCR § 7121(a)
top_risks.description: Secure development and coding practices, oversight of service providers and third parties, and business-continuity and disaster-recovery planning are each rated Implemented (scores 87–89), reflecting operational controls that are in place but whose audit-ready documentation packages have not been confirmed assembled in a form the auditor can examine without further inference. Under 11 CCR § 7122(d), no audit finding may rely primarily on management attestations; the auditor must have access to specific evidence — documents reviewed, sampling and testing performed, and interviews conducted. For secure development, the CI gate-failure reports, SDLC standard (v8, 2026-03-30), and threat-modelling artefacts must be collated. For third-party oversight, the 19 tier-1 executed data-processing agreements and 2026 certificate reviews must be available. For business continuity, the 2026-04-18 failover report and monthly restore-test logs must be retained and accessible.

top_risks.title: Independent documentation of cybersecurity awareness and training as two distinct audit components
top_risks.deadline: Prior to the formal audit engagement; first audit report due by the applicable April 1 phase-in date under 11 CCR § 7121(a)
top_risks.description: If the retained documentation does not separately evidence each component, the auditor cannot assess either independently. The 2026-06-24 briefing deck, KnowBe4 campaign reports, and the 2026-06-30 training completion report provide the underlying substance; the documentation gap is one of separation and labelling, not content.

top_risks.title: Incident record and breach-notification determination retention for the Sev-3 event
top_risks.deadline: We could not verify this item from the information provided; it is listed under information needed.
top_risks.description: The intake reports one security incident in the prior 12 months — a Sev-3 vendor-side exposure closed 2026-02-11 with no personal information involved and three corrective actions completed. The audit report under 11 CCR § 7123(e)(9) and (e)(10) must include, where applicable, sample or descriptive copies of any notifications issued under Cal. Civ. Code § 1798.82(a) and any notifications to California agencies with jurisdiction over privacy laws. The business's documented determination that no personal information was involved — and therefore no notification obligation arose — must itself be retained as audit evidence. The intake records the incident as closed but does not confirm whether the formal no-notification determination has been documented and retained.

next_steps.text: Assemble and make audit-ready the evidence packages for secure development and coding practices, oversight of service providers and third parties, and business-continuity and disaster-recovery planning — specifically: collating the SDLC standard (v8, 2026-03-30), CI gate-failure reports, and threat-modelling artefacts; the 19 tier-1 executed data-processing agreements and 2026 certificate reviews from the OneTrust register; and the 2026-04-18 failover report and monthly restore-test logs — so that the independent auditor has primary documentary evidence for each control under 11 CCR § 7122(d), with all supporting materials retained per the five-year audit-record retention requirement under 11 CCR § 7122(g).

Confirm that the retained documentation for cybersecurity awareness (KnowBe4 campaign reports, 2026-06-24 briefing deck, and security-champions meeting records) and cybersecurity education and training (training standard v4 2026-01-15, 2026-06-30 completion report, and role-based course records) are filed and labelled as separate evidence sets so the auditor can assess each component independently, with both sets retained per the five-year audit-record retention requirement under 11 CCR § 7122(g).

Produce and retain a formal documented determination confirming that the Sev-3 vendor-side exposure closed 2026-02-11 did not involve personal information and did not trigger a notification obligation under Cal. Civ. Code § 1798.82(a) or any California agency notification requirement, and attach this determination to the incident record so the auditor can include or reference the required breach-notification artifact assessment in the audit report under 11 CCR § 7123(e)(9) and (e)(10), retaining the determination and incident record per the five-year audit-record retention requirement under 11 CCR § 7122(g).

authority_exhibit.heading: Appendix — Authorities Cited
authority_exhibit.preamble_note: Verbatim excerpts appear only where the approved corpus carries the text. Where it does not, the citation stands alone.

report.executive_summary: Northwind Clinical Diagnostics Corporation presents a strong cybersecurity readiness posture across all 18 enumerated components under 11 CCR § 7123(c), subject to the auditor's applicability determination. No control presents a Gap or Critical Gap. The prior SOC 2 Type II examination (period 2025-07-01 to 2026-06-30) and ISO 27001 certificate (issued 2025-11-03) are leveraged as permitted under 11 CCR § 7123(f), with segmentation boundaries, retention and disposal, and third-party oversight independently tested. The three highest-priority documentation actions are: (1) assembling audit-ready evidence packages for the three Implemented-rated controls; (2) confirming independent documentation of cybersecurity awareness and training activities as distinct components; and (3) ensuring the incident record and breach-notification determination for the Sev-3 incident are retained as required by 11 CCR § 7123(e). The component tally and its denominator are set out in the component table.

enforcement_context.narrative: Under 11 CCR § 7121(a), first cybersecurity audit reports are due April 1, 2028 for businesses whose 2026 annual gross revenue exceeded $100 million, April 1, 2029 for those with annual gross revenue between $50 million and $100 million, and April 1, 2030 for those with annual gross revenue below $50 million; the business must determine which cohort applies from its actual figures. Clinical diagnostics and patient-results platforms process sensitive health-related personal information at scale, and this sector may attract scrutiny because of the volume and sensitivity of patient data processed and the potential consumer harm from unauthorized access or loss of availability. The formal cybersecurity audit must be performed by a qualified, objective, independent professional who issues an audit report meeting the requirements of 11 CCR § 7123(e); separately, a member of executive management directly responsible for cybersecurity-audit compliance then submits the written certification to the CPPA via cppa.ca.gov under 11 CCR § 7124.

control_status_counts.methodology_note: Component scores are the mean over scored components only. A component recorded as Insufficient information carries no score and is excluded from the mean; it remains in the denominator of eighteen § 7123(c) components.

readiness_determination.headline: On this record the business is ready for a § 7124 certified cybersecurity audit: all 18 § 7123(c) components are implemented and each is supported by testable evidence.
readiness_determination.reasoning: Every enumerated component in § 7123(c) is recorded as implemented, and for each the record identifies at least one testable artefact, so no finding would rest primarily on management assertion under § 7122(d). The engagement is consistent with § 7122, but the record documents rather than demonstrates the auditor's qualifications and retention practice. Nothing on this record prevents an auditor from completing and certifying the audit.

independence_determination.summary: The engagement is consistent with § 7122, but the record documents rather than demonstrates the auditor's qualifications and retention practice.

findings.label: Qualified, objective, independent professional using accepted procedures and standards
findings.standard: Every business required to complete a cybersecurity audit pursuant to this Article must do so using a qualified, objective, independent professional (“auditor”) using procedures and standards accepted in the profession of auditing, such as procedures and standards provided or adopted by the American Institute of Certified Public Accountants, the Public Company Accountability Oversight Board, the Information Systems Audit and Control Association, or the International Organization for Standardization.
findings.application: 11 CCR § 7122(a) requires a qualified, objective, independent professional. The record states an external auditor is engaged with independence confirmed in writing, which evidences the condition.
findings.record_fact: The record states the engagement is: External auditor engaged, independence confirmed in writing.

findings.label: Auditor qualification
findings.standard: To be qualified, an auditor must have knowledge of cybersecurity and how to audit a business’s cybersecurity program.
findings.application: 11 CCR § 7122(a)(1) requires a qualified, objective, independent professional. The record states an external auditor is engaged with independence confirmed in writing, which evidences the condition.
findings.record_fact: The record states the engagement is: External auditor engaged, independence confirmed in writing.

findings.label: Objective and impartial judgment; non-participation in assessed activities
findings.standard: The auditor may be internal or external to the business but must exercise objective and impartial judgment on all issues within the scope of the cybersecurity audit, must be free to make decisions and assessments without influence by the business being audited, including the business’s owners, managers, or employees; and must not participate in activities that may compromise the auditor’s independence.
findings.application: 11 CCR § 7122(a)(2) requires objective and impartial judgment free from influence by the business. The record's engagement description is consistent with that requirement; the arrangement would be confirmed in the engagement letter rather than concluded from the intake alone.
findings.record_fact: The record states the engagement is: External auditor engaged, independence confirmed in writing.

findings.label: Internal-auditor reporting line, performance evaluation, and compensation
findings.standard: If a business uses an internal auditor, to maintain the auditor’s independence, the highest-ranking auditor must report directly to a member of the business’s executive management team who does not have direct responsibility for the business’s cybersecurity program.
findings.application: 11 CCR § 7122(a)(3) applies only where the business uses an internal auditor. This engagement is external, so the reporting-line condition does not bite.
findings.record_fact: The record states the engagement is: External auditor engaged, independence confirmed in writing.

findings.label: No finding may rely primarily on management assertions
findings.standard: No finding of any cybersecurity audit may rely primarily on assertions or attestations by the business’s management. Cybersecurity audit findings must rely primarily upon the specific evidence (including documents reviewed, sampling and testing performed, and interviews conducted) that the auditor deems appropriate.
findings.application: 11 CCR § 7122(d) requires the business and the auditor to retain all documents relevant to each audit for five years. A prior audit is described on the record, so the retention duty is live and the retained set should be identified.
findings.record_fact: The record describes the prior audit scope as: The prior engagement was the SOC 2 Type II examination of the results platform and supporting infrastructure covering security, availability and confidentiality for the period 2025-07-01 to 2026-06-30. It did not cover the laboratory information system interfaces, the retention and disposal controls, or the third-party oversight programme, and it expressed no opinion on compliance with 11 CCR §§ 7121-7124.
findings.information_needed: Confirm where the prior audit's documents are retained and for how long.

findings.label: Five-year retention of audit documents
findings.standard: The business and the auditor must retain all documents relevant to each cybersecurity audit for a minimum of five (5) years after completion of the cybersecurity audit.
findings.application: 11 CCR § 7122(g) requires the business and the auditor to retain all documents relevant to each audit for five years. A prior audit is described on the record, so the retention duty is live and the retained set should be identified.
findings.record_fact: The record describes the prior audit scope as: The prior engagement was the SOC 2 Type II examination of the results platform and supporting infrastructure covering security, availability and confidentiality for the period 2025-07-01 to 2026-06-30. It did not cover the laboratory information system interfaces, the retention and disposal controls, or the third-party oversight programme, and it expressed no opinion on compliance with 11 CCR §§ 7121-7124.
findings.information_needed: Confirm where the prior audit's documents are retained and for how long.
